target_customer: Robotics and physical-AI companies training dexterous manipulation models
problem: Robot learning lacks large-scale data on how human hands touch and grip objects; vision-only datasets miss force and tactile signals.
business_model: Sells tactile plus egocentric-video training data and capture hardware (Skin sensor, Eye2 Pro camera) to robotics labs

founders.name: James Baek
previous_startups: Content creation business (exited, per YC bio)

education: Georgia Tech, BS CS and Economics

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs custom tactile sensor hardware, synchronized egocentric video and a data pipeline; the company says it designs and manufactures its sensors in-house, with a team of 4.

defensibility.rationale: Early; moat would rest on a growing proprietary tactile dataset and hardware know-how, neither shown yet. Other tactile-sensor startups exist (e.g. Contactile, Xense per search results).

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too recent to know; no incumbent action found.

market_need_then: Robotics foundation-model work in 2026 is data-constrained for manipulation; the company positions touch as the missing training modality. Demand evidence beyond company claims not found.
outcome_analysis: 6thSense is a Summer 2026 company at the very start, so no outcome exists yet. It has a small reported pre-seed of about 660 thousand dollars, a technically credible founding team with Tesla, Amazon and DoorDash experience, and a hardware plus data wedge in robotics whose commercial traction is not yet public.
